question: T12 (task-f965eec8e625ed9a, task-d91d6e0d2f550874), after CAP-T12BELOW l and k: once a fall has left the second block on the Scrolling block's top row and columns but with another end row, what does the next growth do to it, and to the phone stack? On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a second Scrolling block added after it, made on the desktop (desktop both 1/2/3/26, phone 1/2/3/10 and 3/2/5/10). v, on the desktop: the first selected, Edit, Design ('open'), presses on Wave Intensity at 150, 0, then 90, Escape (let go, 'go') and three Cmd+Z, a read after each. x, in Mobile View (the frame 428 wide): the second moved onto the top row by two ArrowUp (1/2/3/10 there), then the same steps, then back to Desktop View. R1 ran v x, R2 x v, one edit session each. Nothing saved: every session left by Exit Without Saving.
readsAre: As CAP-T12BELOW. The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('z' is Cmd+Z).
answer: v, desktop: 150 takes both to 1/2/6/26 and 0 leaves the second there as the first goes to 1/2/2/26 (as CAP-T12BELOW l), the section 11 rows. Then 90 takes the first to 1/2/5/26 and stretches the second by the same 3 rows, to 1/2/9/26 (its top stays), the section 14 rows. So a block with the Scrolling block's top row and columns is stretched by the foot's growth whatever its end row.

v, the phone stack (the section made here follows the desktop): 150 and 0 keep the first on top (1/2/3/10, the second 3/2/5/10), though at 0 the first sits inside the second on the desktop; after 90 the second is first (1/2/3/10) and the first under it (3/2/5/10). The step at 0 moved only the Scrolling block; the step at 90 also stretched the second.

x, the phone view, both on 1/2/3/10: 150 takes both to 1/2/7/10, 0 leaves the second there as the first goes to 1/2/2/10, 90 takes the first to 1/2/5/10 and the second to 1/2/10/10, the section 4, 8, 8 then 11 rows. The desktop areas stay (1/2/3/26 both).
Escape keeps every area; each Cmd+Z takes back one step, the phone stack with it. R1 and R2 read alike in every read, apart from Undo and Redo at a plan's start.
Not read: a block on the top row and columns shorter than the Scrolling block; a growth step that moves no other block after one that did (whether the stack then turns); a drag through these steps.

localGuesses.written: before the reads: ours stretched only a block with the exact area, so at 90 it would move the second to 4/2/9/26; and at 0 our phone stack put the second first
